To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cAMP-induced increase of apical Na+ permeability in H441 monolayer is due to the activation of amiloride-sensitive Na+ conductance, and not to the opening of CFTR-type Cl- channels.
cAMP-induced depolarization in H441 confluent epithelia is caused by activation of an amiorlide-sensitive apical Na(+) conductance.
the cAMP-induced increase of Na+ conductance of H441 confluent epithelial monolayers is mediated by an amiloride sensitive ENaC and not by CFTR-type Cl- conductance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electrophysiological properties of human lung epithelial cells.
the study of ion transport in H441 monolayer cells.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the regulation of ion transport across the airway epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the forskolin-induced depol. is due to an increase of Na+ conductance through the apical membrane, which is mediated by ENaC.
the forskolin-induced depolariation of the apical membrane potential of H441 cells is mediated via activation of ENaC channels and not by CFTR.

cAMP stimulation in H441 monolayer cells induces a sustained depolarization of the apical membrane due to the opening of amiloride-sensitive ENaCs, and not due to the opening CFTRs as was suggested by previous authors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cAMP-induced changes in apical membrane potential of H441 monolayer are mediated via activation of amiloride-sensitive Na+ channels.
the apical membrane potential of H441 cells grown as confluent cultures is -43 mV and that cAMP increases Na+ influx by activating ENaC-type channels, but not by activating CFTR-type channels.
the apical membrane potential of H441 cells is depolarized by cAMP and the depolarization is due to activation of ENaC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the apical membrane of H441 cells is permeable to Na+ and that this conductance is activated by forskolin.
forskolin depolarizes the apical membrane potential (Va) of human airway epithelial cells, which is mediated by the activation of the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC).

cAMP-induced changes of Va are not due to Cl- fluxes through CFTR, as previously reported by Verkman and colleagues, and that the apical membrane conductance of H441 cells is dominated by ENaC-type channels.
